title: Making OP50 Solution from Frozen Stock
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vube6sn

steps.title: Prepare LB Agar Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare and sterilize LB agar plates for bacterial growth.

substeps.instruction: Obtain LB Agar from the media kitchen.
Autoclave the agar for 2 hours.
Pour the agar into large petri dishes (60mm).
Leave to dry overnight, then transfer to the cold room.

steps.title: Streak Frozen Sample
steps.instruction: Streak the frozen OP50 sample onto LB agar plates to isolate colonies.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the frozen tube from Freezer 12, SD Box.
Use a sterile pipette tip to collect a frozen sample and streak it onto the LB agar plate.
Use a new pipette tip to streak across the first streak, then streak again at a separate spot.
Repeat the streaking process one more time.
Incubate the plate at 37°C overnight.
Transfer the plate to the fridge the following day (plate remains viable for approximately 1 month).

steps.title: Inoculate LB Broth
steps.instruction: Inoculate LB broth with a single colony for overnight culture.

substeps.instruction: Obtain at least 200ml of LB Broth from the media kitchen.
Transfer the broth into a flat-bottomed conical flask (e.g., 400/500ml flask for 200ml broth to ensure sufficient headspace).
Select and circle a single colony from the culture plate.
Using aseptic technique, scoop the single colony and mix it into the LB Broth in the flask.
Label the flask and incubate on a 37°C shaker overnight.

steps.title: Measure OD and Store Solution
steps.instruction: Quantify the bacterial density and store the resulting solution.

substeps.instruction: Remove the flask from the incubator after overnight incubation.
Measure the OD600 using a spectrophotometer, using LB Broth as the blank.
Record the average OD600 value.
Aliquot the solution into labeled 15ml falcon tubes.
Store the tubes in the 4°C fridge.
